newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka says FRN may be increased.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka says FRN may be increased.

text.p: A roadshow to promote Sri Lanka's $50 million floating rate note (FRN) has been a success and the issue was likely to be increased, Deputy Finance Minister Gamini Lakshman Peiris said on Wednesday.

"The response was very enthusiastic. In all the capitals we visited, we were told that our fundamental economic indictors were very favourable in comparison with other Asian countries," he told reporters.

Sri Lanka's FRN is expected to be launched this month. Citibank International and ING Barings are joint lead managers of the issue, which will have a final maturity of three years and a put option on the second anniversary.
He said Sri Lanka was likely to get "very much more" than the original target of $50 million.
"The exact rate is now being negotiated and we will be able to reach finality within the next few days," he said.
Senior banking sources told Reuters in Colombo that the government expected to get about $75 million.
"Interest in the deal has been very strong and the issue may be increased," a banker familiar with the transaction told Reuters in London last week.
Peiris led a Sri Lankan delegation for the roadshow to Hong Kong, Seoul, Bahrain and London earlier this month.
"It (the visit) was also to take certain preliminary steps with a view to securing a credit rating for Sri Lanka, which we may request before the end of the year," Peiris said.
